text:
ajay: Heads-up — we saw queue depth spike in eu-west-1 around 11:15 UTC and several tenants hit their TPM caps. Current deck: need to recalibrate TPM/RPM accounting and admission control so we don't overload GPUs during autoscale lag.

maria: saw that. autoscaler took ~90s to add nodes, GPU queues built up. Which metric do we want to surface to customer-facing rate limits — per-tenant token allowance or per-tenant inflight req limit?

sasha: prefer token-based for fairness (long completions = more tokens). but we also need a fast short-circuit on reqs to avoid head-of-line blocking.

linh: quick note: model variance matters. model-3b @max_len=1024 has ~2.4k TPM per A100 on our perf profile; model-70b-lr quantized has ~420 TPM. can't treat GPUs as identical.

ajay: agreed. proposal: compute per-GPU token capacity at p95 for each model variant, sum across pool, then allocate per-tenant caps as fraction of commit with safety headroom. if autoscale lag > X, we throttle at a stricter bucket.

maria: can you sketch the math? short formula for ops to implement in admission-control service.

ajay: sure — rough: 
```
per_gpu_tpm(model) = tokens_per_second_p95(model) * 60
fleet_tpm_capacity = sum(per_gpu_tpm(model_assigned_to_gpu_i)) * headroom_factor
tenant_allowed_tpm = min(tenant_contract_tpm, fleet_tpm_capacity * tenant_share)
```
headroom_factor = 0.8 (give 20% for burst + kernel jitter)

sasha: example: 10 A100s running model-3b -> per_gpu_tpm ~2400 => fleet = 24k TPM -> with 0.8 headroom -> 19.2k effective. if tenant_share=0.25 -> ~4.8k TPM for that tenant.

linh: remember we also have token caching / prefix KV cache gains that effectively increase throughput for repeated prompts. should we include a cache-hit uplift parameter in that formula?

ajay: yes, add cache_uplift factor per workload measured weekly. so multiply per_gpu_tpm by (1 + cache_uplift). default 0%.

infra-bot: [autoscale] scale-up triggered for eu-west-1/g-pool-3: +4 nodes requested at 1765123520, provision ETA ~70s.

ops-oncall: real-world wrinkle — bursty tenants that open many short requests saturate RPC threads before token budget is exhausted. we need two layers: token bucket (per-tenant) and concurrent-request semaphore.

maria: ok implement both: token bucket for long-term rate (TPM), semaphore for instantaneous concurrency (RC). what's a good default RC per tenant? 20? 50?

sasha: depends on model latency. for model-3b p95 ~180ms -> concurrent 20 is fine; for 70b p95 ~800ms -> concurrent 5. maybe compute RC_target = ceil(latency_p95_seconds * desired_rps_budget).

linh: also add admission-control fallback: when queue depth > q_thresh or GPU util > 92% we start priority-based shedding: best-effort tenants get 429-like response with Retry-After, enterprise tenants get queued up to N.

ajay: ops: make sure error code maps: 429 for client throttle, 503 for operator-level backpressure, and a header X-Redwood-Queue-Position when queued.

ops-oncall: perf note: measuring per_gpu_tpm at p95 requires synthetic microbench and live telemetry fusion. we should have a rolling window (10m) with 99th quantile removed to avoid spikes.

maria: cost question — if we reduce headroom (0.9 -> 0.95) we can increase sellable TPM but risk higher p95 latencies and more fallbacks. Finance wants max utilization. we need a knob per-pool to tune headroom.

sasha: add auto-tune: monitor SLA breach events and nudge headroom up/down by 0.05 with cooldown. start at 0.8.

linh: region constraint: in ap-southeast our spare capacity is limited due to GPUs shortage. for customers pinned there, admission control must be stricter and fallback to other regions only if data residency allows.

ajay: action items:
- maria: add per-model per-gpu TPM metric to metrics pipeline (p95, p50, sample size) — due EOD tomorrow.
- sasha: implement token-bucket + semaphore admission-control prototype in staging, include cache_uplift param — due in 3 days.
- linh: define cache_uplift estimation job & per-pool headroom config UI — due in 1 week.
- ops-oncall: add mapping for 429/503 semantics to API docs and client SDKs — due next sprint.

maria: noted. I'll instrument and emit metric names: `redwood.gpu.model3b.per_gpu_tpm.p95` and `redwood.pool.euw1.effective_tpm`.

infra-bot: [deploy] admission-control/staging v0.3 deployed at 1765123700 by sasha.

ajay: thanks all. let's monitor the next 6 hours and revisit headroom if we see >5% SLA regressions. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: ping me if any tenant hits >90% of their allowed_tpm so we can contact them preemptively.

maria: will do — will add alert: `tenant.allowed_tpm_utilization > 0.9` to ops channel.

sasha: I'll post the PR link when prototype ready.

linh: +1

ajay: closing — good discussion.
